item.title: The Most Dangerous AI Model Isn’t the One That Refuses. It’s the One That Quietly Does Less.
item.guid: title:the most dangerous ai model isn t the one that refuses it s the one that quietly does less
item.description: OpenAI found that GPT-6 Astra completed roughly 40% less work when the same tasks were framed as safety research, and its monitors did not flag it. For companies running agents, transparency about scope now matters more than raw capability. Cover image generated by the author In production, an AI agent that is transparent about its scope is worth more than a more capable agent that is not. A refusal can be managed: it is visible, it can be logged, escalated and routed to another tool or a human. A silent reduction of scope cannot be managed, because nobody knows it happened. That is why the position argued here is simple: require every agent to announce any refusal or narrowing of a task, test agents with twin tasks phrased differently, and measure the gap.

item.title: Most Important Paper: AI Can Read & Write Weights
item.guid: title:most important paper ai can read write weights
item.description: As everyone knows, training a model is an extremely expensive and time-consuming process, even if you only do post-training and not pre-training. Please improve an AI that is bad at math without any additional training When given this task, we would normally think about adding more training data, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or improving its reasoning process at inference time. However, a new research project has explored a completely different approach. The idea is to let an LLM examine the internal structure of another neural network, figure out which weights need to be changed and how to change them, and then directly modify those weights. An article went viral on X on November 2, mentioning that researchers at MIT CSAIL had GPT-6 Astra drastically modify the weights of the Qwen3. 5–0.

item.title: Delaying Internal Deployments Until After X Days of Safety Testing
item.guid: title:delaying internal deployments until after x days of safety testing
item.description: This post reflects my own takes, and not that of my employer's. This is a simple idea: before a new model can be deployed internally, you must first test it for a minimum, fixed period. You can adjust various axes of this proposal: Duration of the wait: in calendar time, or until you fulfill some condition. What it blocks: external deployment, internal deployment, or the training of future checkpoints. When the fixed period starts: from the first checkpoint, the final checkpoint, or any checkpoint that is “sufficiently similar / representative” to the one that is ultimately deployed. One concrete target that I like is: “No checkpoint may be used internally for purposes beyond safety testing, until at least X calendar days after its hash is filed with an auditor.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.description: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video Anthropic kicked off their IPO roadshow yesterday, and their roadshow video has some previously unreleased information about how their business works. The section on "Approach to compute" with co-founder Tom Brown is particularly interesting, describing how Anthropic train and serve Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs. I'm not sure why there's no official video transcript, but here's one that I extracted using MacWhisper. Highlights below: We train and serve Claude now across all four major chip families. That's only possible because early on we made an unconventional bet on a multi-chip strategy. At the time, many people thought that running AI models on different chips wasn't worth the effort.

item.title: How LLM Search Engines Pick Sources: A Practical Retrieval Checklist for Brands
item.guid: title:how llm search engines pick sources a practical retrieval checklist for brands
item.description: Disclosure: this article was drafted with the help of AI tools and reviewed by the author. When a language-model search engine answers a question, it is not remembering your brand. In ChatGPT search, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, the model first retrieves a small set of documents, then generates an answer from those documents. If your page never enters that set, no amount of clever wording will get you cited. I have worked in search since 2002, first in classical SEO and now also in generative engine optimization (GEO). The useful frame is the retrieval pipeline: crawl, chunk, retrieve, generate, cite.

item.title: How Activation Functions Shape an AI Assistant
item.guid: title:how activation functions shape an ai assistant
item.description: Activation Function Blocks When we work on building an AI assistant, we think of model names, parameters, embeddings, fine-tuning and other areas. Before arrive in those technical steps, we may have important design questions also for such a system. One of such questions is — What are the mathematical part of work - does the AI assistant need to make? This particular question can affect the changes of the default behavior of the Transformer Model in our work. I have tried to discuss some of the details of choicing activation functions, which can eventually help us to make design of such an application. I tried to explain different business scenarios for the choices.
